note: Libya: nationals of Algeria, Mauritania and Tunisia enter without a visa for 3 months, Malaysians for 30 days (through Misurata and Mitiga only, a security letter possibly asked: not modelled); everyone else applies for a tourist e-Visa (since 21 March 2024; 30 days, USD 63) through a tour operator or local sponsor, except nationals of Bangladesh, Iran, Pakistan, Sudan, Syria and Yemen, restricted to a visa, and Israelis, refused (taken as a visa). Egypt's and Turkey's age- and sex-bound exemptions and Belarus's doubtful one aren't modelled. Read from Wikipedia's copy. Checked on 2026-11-03 against the e-Visa service's own country list and eligibility check: it confirmed the four exempt and no row for Israel, but offers the e-Visa to Bangladeshis, Iranians, Pakistanis, Sudanese, Syrians and Yemenis, so those six were moved to the e-Visa, and marks South Sudan, Taiwan, Kosovo and Western Sahara unavailable, so those four were moved to a visa (refused). The stays and the fee aren't given by the service and stand on Wikipedia's copy.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Visa policy of Libya
sources.said: Visitors to Libya must obtain a visa from one of the Libyan diplomatic missions or an e-Visa unless they are citizens from one of the visa-exempt countries. ... may enter Libya without a visa for the following period: 3 months Algeria Mauritania Tunisia 30 days Malaysia ... Libya launched an e-Visa system on 21 March 2024. Tourist e-Visa is valid for 90 days and good for single entry, it allows applicant from most countries to stay no more than 30 days by paying a 63 USD fee. ... Citizens of the following countries are restricted to get the visa to enter Libya: Bangladesh Iran Pakistan Sudan Syria Yemen ... Entry and transit is banned to citizens of Israel
